title: 10 most frequent words in a text
description:
Read this url and find the 10 most frequent words. romeo_and_juliet = 'http://www.gutenberg.org/files/1112/1112.txt'

Python-Gym adaptation: this exercise is about downloading a live text file with `requests` and analysing it, which the grading sandbox cannot do (no network access, and the remote file may move or disappear). Implement as `top_10_words(text)`, taking the already-downloaded text as a string parameter instead of fetching the URL, and return the 10 most frequent words as a list of `(word, count)` tuples ordered from most to least frequent, exactly as `collections.Counter(...).most_common(10)` would produce.
examples:
>>> top_10_words("one two two three three three")
[('three', 3), ('two', 2), ('one', 1)]
starter_code:
def top_10_words(text):
    # write your code here
    # tokenize text into lowercase words (letters and apostrophes only)
    # and return the 10 most common (word, count) pairs
    pass
hints: Lowercase the text first so 'The' and 'the' count as the same word.
Use a regular expression like re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text.lower()) to pull out words while ignoring punctuation and digits.
collections.Counter has a .most_common(n) method that returns exactly the (word, count) tuples you need, already sorted by frequency.
expected_behavior: Returns a list of up to 10 (word, count) tuples, the most frequent words in text first, where words are compared case-insensitively and punctuation is ignored. On empty or whitespace-only text, returns an empty list.

hidden_tests.call:
top_10_words("Two households, both alike in dignity,
In fair Verona, where we lay our scene,
From ancient grudge break to new mutiny,
Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean.
From forth the fatal loins of these two foes
A pair of star-cross'd lovers take their life;
Whose misadventured piteous overthrows
Do with their death bury their parents' strife.
The fearful passage of their death-mark'd love,
And the continuance of their parents' rage,
Which, but their children's end, nought could remove,
Is now the two hours' traffic of our stage;
The which if you with patient ears attend,
What here shall miss, our toil shall strive to mend.")
hidden_tests.label: opening lines of Romeo and Juliet's prologue

hidden_tests.call: top_10_words("The cat sat on the mat. The cat was happy. A dog saw the cat and the dog barked at the cat.")
hidden_tests.label: fewer than 10 distinct words returns all of them

hidden_tests.call: top_10_words("one two two three three three")
hidden_tests.label: example from the description
empty text returns an empty list

explanation: re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+", text.lower()) tokenizes the lowercased text into runs of letters and apostrophes, stripping out punctuation and digits as separators. Counter then tallies how many times each word occurs, and .most_common(10) returns the ten highest counts as (word, count) tuples, sorted from most to least frequent (ties keep the order in which the word was first seen).
